problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $X$ and $Y$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(X)=-8$, find $det(Y).$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}],\,Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

mathematical_assessment.explanation: Rechecking confirms the contradiction: the displayed X has determinant 5 and Y has determinant -5. Swapping rows 2 and 3 negates the determinant, so the stated det(X) = -8 instead implies 8 (option b). The earlier uncertainty remains because these premises disagree, and -5 is absent from the choices.

activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants
